Mr. Mizanur Rahman, Advocate ------ For the opposite party No. 1

JLM Container Service Ltd. 28 Sarson Road, North Hill Estate, Kotwali, Chittagong
Vs.
Md. Golam Sarwar
full_judgment:
Sheikh Abdul Awal, J: This Rule was issued calling upon the petitioner-opposite party to show cause as to why the impugned Judgment and order dated 6.5.2014 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, Bankruptcy Court, Chittagong in Arbitration Misc. Case No.181 of 2013 allowing the Misc. Case under section 12 of the Arbitration Act, 2001 and thereby directing the petitioner to supply the name and address of the arbitrator for and on behalf of him by 30.6.2014 should not be set-aside. 

 The opposite party as petitioner filed Arbitration Misc. Case No.181 of 2013 before the learned District Judge under section 12 of the Arbitration Act, 2001 on the allegation that the opposite party entered into a contract on 28.11.2012 with the petitioner for the purpose of transporting Siemen's Project N-000030 equipments (Transformers and shunt Reactors) of 500 MW Power Plant sub-station located at Bheramara. Ultimately, as per the said contract, the opposite party was to transport three shipments and accordingly the opposite party took all necessary preparation by arranging suitable tugs and water crafts but in violation of the contract, the petitioner used other service providers for the 2nd shipment. In this background the opposite party served a legal notice on 7.01.2013 claiming compensation for the losses caused by the breach of contract in which the petitioner agreed in reply to the legal notice dated 10.01.2013 and requested for arranging a meeting to discuss the dispute for amicable settlement. Thereupon, the lawyer of the opposite party vide notice dated 17.01.2013 requested the lawyer of the petitioner for sitting and accordingly a meeting was held on 29.01.2013 at German Club, Gulshan, Dhaka wherein it was agreed to pay compensation to the opposite party in which the opposite party asked for a security before final delivery of the Cargo from the said vessel but the petitioner by taking different pleas avoided to furnish any security. Thereafter, on 21.3.2013 the petitioner took control of the DB Labiba with the help of local mastans/miscreants and berthed the Barge and forcefully discharged the cargo on 26.3.2013 without paying all dues under the contract and settlement agreement as well. The contract dated 28.11.2012 contains a clause for Arbitration, that is, "If any parties violate this agreement, it will be settled as per arbitration Law in Bangladesh." In this backdrop, since a dispute has been cropped up between the parties to the said contract dated 28.11.2012 due to violation of the terms and conditions, the opposite party by appointing its arbitrator sent a notice dated 21.7.2013 to the petitioner for nominating its arbitrator within 30 days as per provision of Arbitration Act, 2001 but the petitioner did not nominate its arbitrator and hence, the case under section 12 of the Arbitration Act, 2001. 

 3. Petitioner-opposite party resisted the Arbitration Misc. Case under section 12 of the Arbitration Act, 2001 by filing written objection denying most of the allegation contending, inter-alia, that the Misc. Case itself is not maintainable in its present form and manner inasmuch as the case is barred by principle of waiver, estopple and acquiescence and also barred by limitation. The Misc. Case is bad for defect of parties and hence the same is liable to be rejected. 

 4. Ultimately, the said Arbitration Misc. Case was transferred to the Court of learned Additional District Judge, Bankruptcy Court, Chittagong for disposal, who after hearing by the impugned Judgment and order dated 6.5.2014 allowed the Misc. Case and the instant civil revision is directed against that judgment and order. 

 5. Mr. A. B. M. Siddiqur Rahman, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite party-petitioner submits that the learned Additional District Judge and Bankruptcy Court, Chittagong erred in law in allowing the misc. case under section 12 of the Arbitration Act without considering the facts and circumstance of the case and the case made out by the opposite party-petitioner that JLM Container Services Ltd. is the agent of Panalpina and actually the agreement was made between Fast stream and Panalpina through JLM Container Services Ltd. and as such, Panalpina should do the needful for appointing its arbitrator although in this case Panalpina was not made party and thus fell into an error of law in allowing the Misc. case which resulted in the failure of justice. He next submits that the opposite party issued legal notice upon 4 parties including Panalpina although the opposite party herein as petitioner in the misc. case under section 12 of the Arbitration Act only impleaded the instant opposite party-petitioner, who in the facts and circumstance of the case is nobody to appoint any arbitrator in favour of Panlpina whatsoever. He further submits that the agreement in question is an international agreement and as such in entertaining the Misc. Case the learned District Judge, Chittagong traveled beyond his jurisdiction. The learned Advocate further submits that the Panalpina is willing to add as party in the instant Misc. Case in order to do the needful and under such facts and circumstance unless the Panalpina is added as a party in the case the present opposite party-petitioner will suffer irreparable loss and injury but the learned Additional District Judge, Bankruptcy Court, Chittagong without considering all these vital aspects of the case arbitrarily allowed the Misc. Case under section 12 of the Arbitration Act which resulted in the failure of justice. 

 7. Heard the learned Advocates for both the sides and perused the revision application, counter affidavit dated 02.5.2015 and affidavit in reply to the counter affidavit and other relevant papers as filed thereto. Now, to deal with the contentions raised by the parties before me it would be convenient for me to decide first of all the question of maintainability of the Misc. Case under section 12 of the Arbitration Act preferred by the opposite party. 

 8. On scrutiny of the record, it appears that the agreement was made between Fast stream Logistic Ltd. as party and JLM Container Services Ltd. as 2nd party place on 28.11.2012. From the petition of the Misc. Case, it appears that the opposite party herein as petitioner, Md. Golam Sarwar, son of late Abul Kashem, Managing Director, Fast stream Logistics Ltd., Aktaruzzaman Centre (7th Floor) 21/22, Agrabad C/A, Chittagong, Bangladesh filed the instant Misc. Case under section 12 of the Arbitration Act. 

 9. Therefore, I find no difficulty whatever in holding that Mr. A. B. M. Siddiqur Rahman, is not correct in submitting that Md. Golam Sarwar as a 3rd party filed the Misc. Case under section 12 of the Arbitration Act and as such the same is not tenable in law. My view is, therefore, that the Misc. Case under section 12 of the Arbitration Act filed by the Managing Director of Fast stream Logistics Ltd. under section 12 of the Arbitration Act is well maintainable as the Misc. case appears to have filed by the competent authority in the light of agreement as evidenced by "Annexure-F" to the revisional application. 

 10. On perusal of the agreement in question, it appears that the addresses of both the parties as mentioned therein at Agrabad, Chittagong. Therefore, the plea as canvassed by Mr. A. B. M. Siddiqur Rahman that the learned Additional District Judge, Chittagong travelled beyond his jurisdiction in entertaining the Misc. Case under section 12 of the Arbitration Act as the agreement in question is an international agreement does not find any legs to stand upon. 

 11. It further appears that the agreement in question was executed by Fast stream Logistic Ltd. as 10 party and JLM Container Services Ltd. as 3rd party and Mr. Md. Golam Sarwar, the Managing Director, Fast stream Logistics Ltd as petitioner justly filed the Misc. Case under section 12 of the Arbitration Act impleading the JLM Container Services Ltd. as sole opposite party. Therefore, in the facts and circumstance of the case, I am unable to see eye to eye to such submission of Mr. A. B. M. Siddiqur Rahman that the Misc. case was bad for defect of parties. 

 12. Now, it remains me to consider the last submission of Mr. A. B. M. Siddiqur Rahman that Panalpina is willing to add as opposite party in the instant misc. case for and on behalf of the JLM Container Services Ltd. for doing the needful. 

 13. In the facts and circumstances of the case and law bearing on the subject this submission is plainly misconceived. 

 15. On a scrutiny of the impugned judgment, I find that the learned Additional District Judge, Chittagong after a detailed discussion of the attending facts and circumstances borne out by records rightly held that the Misc. Case is not bad for defect of parties and the same is well tenable in law. The learned Additional District Judge, Chittagong appears to have considered all the material aspects of the case and justly allowed the Misc. Case under section 12 of the Arbitration Act, I find no reason to interfere therewith.
